items.a: Mobility needs **structure, a measure and progressive overload**, just like strength.

items.q: How do you make dislocates progressive?
items.a: Move the grip **slightly closer every rep** and log the width you reach.

items.q: How should a standing backbend start?
items.a: Bum out, **chest to the ceiling first**, then lean back, so the bend comes from the upper back.

items.q: How do you protect the lower back?
items.a: **Squeeze the glutes** (posterior pelvic tilt) and stop the lumbar spine doing all the bending.

items.q: What forearm angle should a back bridge have?
items.a: About **90° to the floor**. Raise the feet until you get there.
Touch the wall with **head, then nose, then chin, then chest**.
**Up on the toes, touch the point, lower the heels** while holding it.

items.q: When should you train these drills?
items.a: As **strength work** a couple of times a week, **not as a warm-up**.
